newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Vanishing Aral Sea to be focus of Kazakhstan summit.
newsitem.headline: Vanishing Aral Sea to be focus of Kazakhstan summit.

text.p: The vanishing Aral Sea, one of the former Soviet Union's worst ecological disasters, will be the focus of a five-nation Central Asian summit next week, the Kazakh government said on Friday.

"The leaders of Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan will meet the (Kazakh) president next Friday," a spokesman for President Nursultan Nazarbayev told Reuters. The summit will be held in the Kazakh capital, Almaty.

Wasteful irrigation projects to boost Central Asian cotton production in the Soviet era have seen the inland sea's volume drop by about three quarters since the 1960s, killing the fishing industry and creating severe health problems in the area.
But conservation is hampered by the Central Asian states' continued need for water from the mighty Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers, which feed into the Aral Sea.

Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan still rely on cotton exports for hard currency and both countries want to be self-sufficient in grain, for which their land -- much of it desert -- requires large amounts of irrigation.
